title: AWS Config: Compliance & Inventory 📋
description: Continuously evaluate and audit your resource configurations against desired policies.

slides.title: What is AWS Config? 📋
slides.content:
# The Configuration State Recorder

AWS Config continuously monitors and records your resource configurations. It captures:
- **Resource inventory** – what resources exist.
- **Configuration changes** – a history of every change (who changed it, when, what changed).
- **Relationships** – how resources are connected (e.g., this EC2 instance uses that security group).

It answers questions like "Did someone open port 22 to the world on our production security group last Tuesday?"

**Analogy**: Config is like a time‑lapse camera pointed at your infrastructure. It takes a snapshot whenever something changes, so you can rewind and see the exact state at any moment.

quizData.question: How does AWS Config differ from AWS CloudTrail?

options.text: Config records API calls; CloudTrail records resource state
Config records resource configurations and changes over time; CloudTrail records API calls
Config monitors performance; CloudTrail monitors compliance

quizData.explanation: Config focuses on 'what is the state of my resource?' and its history. CloudTrail records 'who called what API?'.

slides.title: Rules: Evaluate Compliance ✅
slides.content:
# Automated Guardrails

Config Rules are policies that check whether resources match desired configurations. You can use:
- **AWS Managed Rules** (e.g., `s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited`, `restricted-ssh`, `encrypted-volumes`).
- **Custom Rules** (Lambda functions that evaluate resources programmatically).

Rules are evaluated when:
- A resource is created or changed (triggered)
- Periodically (e.g., every 24 hours)

Results are marked as **COMPLIANT** or **NON_COMPLIANT** and can trigger automatic remediation.

slides.title: Remediation: Auto‑Fix Drift 🔧
slides.content:
# Self‑Healing Infrastructure

Config Rules can be paired with **automatic remediation actions** using SSM Automation documents. For example:
- Rule: `encrypted-volumes` → if non‑compliant, automatically run SSM document to encrypt the EBS volume.
- Rule: `s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited` → automatically apply Block Public Access.

This closes the loop from detection to resolution without human intervention.

slides.title: Conformance Packs: Compliance at Scale 📦
slides.content:
# Bundled Best Practices

A conformance pack is a collection of Config Rules and remediation actions that you can deploy as a single unit. AWS provides packs aligned with industry standards (PCI DSS, HIPAA, CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark).

You can deploy a pack across your entire organization using AWS Organizations, ensuring consistent security posture.

slides.title: Pro Tip: Start with CIS Benchmarks 🚀
slides.content:
## Deploy Pre‑built Conformance Pack

The CIS AWS Foundations Benchmark conformance pack contains over 40 rules. Deploy it to instantly evaluate your account against industry best practices. It's a great baseline for any new account.
